2026.clinched: London E-Prix, ExCeL, 16 August 2026, final round (17 of 17)
2026.note: Nine drivers could still have won the 2026 title when the season reached London, with the top three inside five points, and it stayed open until the last half hour of the last race. Wehrlein had won Saturday's round from Jake Dennis, then started third on Sunday with Dennis sixteenth. He was shuffled back to twelfth as Dennis climbed into a virtual championship lead, until Dennis hit Joel Eriksson at Turn 16 on lap 31 and retired with the damage. Taylor Barnard won the race, at 22 the youngest winner in the series' history. Wehrlein took the championship by five points from Dennis, his second after 2024, while Jaguar TCS Racing kept the teams' title.

2025.clinched: Berlin E-Prix, 13 July 2025, two rounds to spare (round 14 of 16)
2025.note: Rowland arrived in Berlin 69 points clear and needed to leave it 58 clear, which fourth place in the second Berlin race did comfortably, even after a five-place grid penalty carried over from a crash the day before. Nick Cassidy won the race, Jake Dennis was second and Jean-Éric Vergne third, but the title went to the Nissan driver on 184 points against Pascal Wehrlein's 125. Four wins and seven podiums made it his first championship, and the first time since 2020 that the drivers' title had not run to the London finale.

2024.clinched: London E-Prix, 21 July 2024, final round (16 of 16)
2024.note: Seven drivers could still have won it when the season reached London, and Wehrlein was third of them, twelve points behind Nick Cassidy. He won Saturday's race to take the lead back, then finished second on Sunday behind Oliver Rowland, with Mitch Evans third, and that was the championship. It was Porsche's first title in Formula E and it came from consistency rather than speed: three wins, five podiums, and points in all but two of the sixteen races.

2023.clinched: London E-Prix, 29 July 2023, one round to spare (round 15 of 16)
2023.note: Dennis went to his home race 24 points clear of Nick Cassidy, who started from pole, and left it champion with a race in hand. The London race was stopped twice; Cassidy lost his front wing in contact with his own team-mate Sébastien Buemi, pitted, recovered to sixteenth and then retired. Dennis crossed the line third and was promoted to second behind the winner Mitch Evans, which settled it. It was a first world title for him and for Andretti, at a circuit where he had already won twice.

2022.clinched: Seoul E-Prix, 14 August 2022, final round (16 of 16)
2022.note: Vandoorne started fourth and finished second in Seoul, in the hundredth race Formula E had run, and took the title 33 points clear of Mitch Evans. Evans had needed to win from thirteenth on the grid with Vandoorne eighth or lower, and got as far as seventh. Vandoorne won only once all season, at Monaco, against four apiece for Evans and Edoardo Mortara, but he failed to score in only one race and led the standings for most of the year. It was Mercedes' last race in the series before the team was sold to McLaren, and its second title in a row.

2021.clinched: Berlin E-Prix, 15 August 2021, final round (15 of 15)
2021.note: Fourteen drivers still had a mathematical chance when the last race of 2021 started, and de Vries won the championship by finishing eighth in it. His own weekend had been dreadful: nineteenth on the grid for Saturday's race and a puncture that dropped him to twenty-second, cutting his lead to a single point. On Sunday, Mitch Evans stalled at the start and Edoardo Mortara hit him, taking out two contenders; Jake Dennis then hit the wall at the first corner after the restart. Norman Nato won the race. De Vries finished on 99 points, seven clear of Mortara, as Formula E's first FIA-recognised World Champion.

2020.clinched: Berlin E-Prix, 9 August 2020, two rounds to spare (round 9 of 11)
2020.note: Da Costa followed his DS Techeetah team-mate Jean-Éric Vergne home at Tempelhof, second place giving him a 76-point lead with only 60 still available: at the time, no Formula E driver had ever won the title with two rounds to spare. The season had been interrupted for five months by the pandemic and finished with six races in nine days at a disused Berlin airport, no spectators, mandatory testing, and a different track layout for each pair of races. His three consecutive wins in mid-season included the first grand slam in the championship's history.

2019.clinched: New York City E-Prix, 14 July 2019, final round (13 of 13)
2019.note: Vergne needed only to stay out of trouble in Brooklyn and finished seventh, which made him the first driver to defend a Formula E title. Three drivers had arrived with a chance: Lucas di Grassi 22 points behind and Mitch Evans 25, and the two of them collided and crashed on the last lap. Robin Frijns won the race from Alexander Sims and Sébastien Buemi. Vergne ended the season on 136 points to Buemi's 119, and DS Techeetah took its first teams' championship.

2018.clinched: New York City E-Prix, 14 July 2018, one round to spare (round 11 of 12)
2018.note: This was the first Formula E title that did not go to the final race. Vergne and his team-mate had been sent to the back of the grid for turning their power up too early in qualifying; he climbed to fifth while his only rival Sam Bird finished ninth, which left a 31-point lead with one race remaining. Lucas di Grassi won the race, on Bastille Day, and Vergne became the first French champion of the series and its fourth different champion in four seasons. He took four wins from twelve rounds and 198 points, 54 clear of di Grassi.

2017.clinched: Montreal E-Prix, 30 July 2017, final round (12 of 12)
2017.note: Di Grassi went to Montreal ten points behind Sébastien Buemi and came home champion, and the weekend turned before either race: Buemi crashed heavily in practice, his team rebuilt the car in under five hours, and he took a ten-place grid penalty for it. Di Grassi won Saturday's race from pole while Buemi recovered to fourth and was then disqualified for an underweight car, which turned a ten-point deficit into an eighteen-point lead. Seventh place on Sunday was enough, in a race won by Jean-Éric Vergne, the first for the Techeetah team. Buemi finished the year 24 points adrift.

2016.clinched: London E-Prix, Battersea Park, 3 July 2016, final round (10 of 10)
2016.note: Buemi and Lucas di Grassi arrived at Battersea Park level on points, with di Grassi ahead on a count-back of results, and the pair took each other out on the first lap: di Grassi ran into the back of Buemi at Turn 3 and both cars hit the wall. A double retirement would have handed di Grassi the title on that count-back, so the championship came down to the two points awarded for the fastest lap. Both limped on at the back of the field waiting for clear air. Di Grassi set his time first and Buemi beat it, taking the title 155 points to 153.

2015.clinched: London E-Prix, Battersea Park, 28 June 2015, final round (11 of 11)
2015.note: The first Formula E season, run from September 2014, was decided by one point. Piquet Jr. qualified sixteenth after a wet session and was told by his team not to ask where his rivals were, just to drive; he finished seventh. Sébastien Buemi, who had won the day before and started sixth, spun on cold tyres after his car change and came out behind Bruno Senna, and taking fourth place off Senna on the last lap would have given him the championship instead. He could not. Piquet Jr. finished on 144 points to Buemi's 143, with two wins that year, at Long Beach and Moscow.
